utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is Thursday, June 5th, 2008. I would like to greet the representatives of the OTP, Mr. Seselj, the Registrar, and everyone helping us, notably the interpreters. The hearing is starting a bit late, 45 minutes late. It was scheduled for 8.30. Mr. Seselj, do you have any idea why we're so late?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reason is a trivial one, Mr. President. Late last night, when they were locking up, I was told that the transport would be at 7.45. They tell me every evening when I will be transported the next day. However, today at 7.25 the guard came by and said that the transport was arranged for 7.30. Now, I wasn't able to finish my toilet in five minutes, I needed eleven minutes. So at 7.36, I was ready. However, the Dutch police had already left. I suppose they had somebody else at that same time and didn't want to wait for me. So that's the only reason. Afterwards, everything took its turn, and when they finished everything else, they came to fetch me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will ask the Dutch police for explanations. I will ask them why they left, whereas their mission was to drive you, even if you were a bit late. But we will now resume the hearing of our witness. We need the blinds to be dropped because of the protective measures that were granted. Mr. Seselj, you have one hour and fifteen minutes left for this cross-examination. The Registrar just told me that you have one hour and forty-five minutes left. I had cut you short by 30 minutes, but I do hope that we will finish on time with this witness. We are in Courtroom II because other trials are sitting in Courtroom I and Courtroom III, and these trials could only be accommodated in these two other courtrooms, which is why exceptionally we're sitting in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Our apologies for this late start. There was, unfortunately, a logistical problem, and because of that we were delayed, slightly delayed, which is why you had to wait for this hearing to start, just like we did. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Witness VS-1055, we're now going to deal with your first statement for a bit, the one you gave to the State Security Service, and then later on to the Municipal Centre for Research into War Crimes which was dislocated [as interpreted] to Breza. In the first part of that statement, and may we have the statement on the overhead projector, please, for the witness to be able to see it on his screen. Anyway, in the first part of that statement you speak about general political conditions and circumstances in Ljesevo before the war broke out, and you talk about the events in the Serbian Democratic Party, and the Serbian Democratic Party is the one you blame for everything that happened later on, in fact, because you say that the Serb extremists were the core of the extremist organisation of the Serb population. You name names. They were local functionaries of the Serbian Democratic Party. And you speak about the Crisis Staff that was set up for Ljesevo. But there's not a word here -- have we got it on our screens now, page 1 of the statement? No, we haven't. I think that the Prosecution should have a copy for the witness to use, not to have to answer questions off the top of his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a reoccurring issue. The accused is to come prepared for his cross-examination. If he wants to use statements, he really should bring them. He has been provided by the Tribunal with logistical support, and he has a big -- and we have also provided a copy -- but the court officer, I think, has been a provided a copy and would help, but I do think Your Honours should direct the accused to prepare his own documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have prepared all my own documents, but in just one copy, and I don't intend preparing other copies. It's 0338-0381 is the ERN number, and it's your duty to prepare the document for our screens. All I'm obliged to do is to state the number. I have no intention nor do I have the possibilities of photocopying documents, and I don't want to prepare you for stating the documents I'm going to use that you disclose to me. So this is a previous statement by this witness, and that must be available in the courtroom. And you must have disclosed it in that binder of yours so that the Judges could have it before them, but you failed to do that, so that the Judges can follow the witness statement and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on, Mr. Seselj. We'll not waste any time. You're giving us a document with an ERN number. Theoretically, if the document was up-loaded in e-court, it should be found using that number, but this is theoretical, of course. Of course, unfortunately practice is more complicated than theory.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we going to have that pulled up on our screens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We now have it on the screen. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As I was saying, I summarised the introduction of your statement, not to waste time on the details, so I'm now asking you, Mr. VS-1055, what was the first national party that was organised in Bosnia-Herzegovina on the eve of the toppling of the communist regime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was -- the party that was founded first might have been the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That party was organised months before the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the Party of Democratic Action, the SDA, already in 1981, had formed an organisation called the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: 1991. Do you know that the Patriotic League had its paramilitaries called the Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard about that; okay. So at the very least, your representations here, that it was only the Serbian Democratic Party that was to blame, is just a one-sided view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about Bosnia-Herzegovina. I was talking about my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, in your village, did the SDA party exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did exist, but there were no Green Berets or whatever you called them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You didn't have any Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But the SDA party did exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that party armed at least a part of the Muslim population on the territory of Ilijas municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in the house of somebody you know very well is where that party was formed? I don't want to mention his name, not to have any problems and have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like you to name names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't want to name the name now, or could we just go into private session for a few seconds, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly be asked once again to slow down, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your statement, somewhere in the middle of the first paragraph, you go on to say that the Serbian Democratic Party started to prepare a Chetnik organisation as well, is that right, and that it began arming the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, it did begin arming the Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The weapons arrived from Ilijas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the weapons arrived from Ilijas, but I mention the weapons coming from Josipovic, who it was the commander of the barracks, and he pulled them out from Ljesevo, Malesic, Cekrcici, [Indiscernible], handed the weapons around to the Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that was when the JNA withdrew from Visoko; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was moving out of Visoko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You are aware that everything you are saying is being interpreted into English and French. The interpreters are unable to follow the speed of your conversation with the accused, so I kindly ask you to observe a short pause between the question before you start answering. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I got carried away. I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In that first paragraph, you speak about all the events that took place at Ilijas municipality which were before the clash of the 4th of June, isn't that right, and you're looking at it in a one-sided way? The Serbian Democratic Party you said organised the Chetniks, will arm the population, the JNA supplying weapons to the Serbs. That is the point of what you say there; right? Am I right when I say that, Mr. VS-1055?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do we have to read that whole paragraph or can we make the conclusion that its basic contents are contained in those three points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The first paragraph, the long first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about Ljesevo here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The whole of Ilijas. Do we have to read it all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's read it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You want everything read out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the vital points, as far as you're concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I have extracted the vital points, and it is this: That you claim that it was the Serbian Democratic Party, led by extremists, and that it organised the Chetniks, and that the JNA provided the Serbs with weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's the substance of that paragraph of yours. You mention many people, Serbs who, in your opinion, took part in all that; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Right. Now, there is no mention here by you of the fact that Vasilije Vidovic, nicknamed Vaske, brought in 20 armed men, volunteers, from Knin to Ilijas. There's none of that here, and that was the most important piece of information which you provided to the Court during the examination-in-chief. So why did you not tell your police that Vaske Vidovic brought in 20 armed Chetniks to Ilijas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remain -- I stand by my statement of yesterday, when I said that Vasilije Vidovic had a group of men, 20 or more people, in Ilijas and that that group attacked my village. Now, why I did not make that statement, I don't really know why I didn't say that, but I don't think that I was tardy in responding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're not answering my question. Did the arrival of 20 men from Knin, armed Chetniks -- was that sufficient -- a sufficiently important piece of information that you had to tell the Muslim police that, but you failed to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't say I didn't say it. They all saw it, they all knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, they must have known everything else that you told them about, but nonetheless you told them about it. They knew all these officials of the Serb Democratic Party better than you did, the ones you told them about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, why would they need your statement, then, in which you mention Aleksandar Rostovic, Kojo Glisic, Trivko Radic, Nedzo Boskovic, Dusko Balordas [phoen], Slobodan Glisic, Bozo Boskovic and so on, a lot of names, Ratko Kakuca? Why would they need all that information and there's no Vaske Vidovic with his 20 Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. Mr. Seselj, I have a problem. In order to understand or to assess whether the testimony this witness gave yesterday is in compliance with the statement or not, I need to have the statement in English. Otherwise, you're having a private conversation with the witness, you're challenging what he is saying, but I cannot take this into account. I'm not able to know what's really going on. I don't know how to solve the problem. Maybe you should have asked the CLSS to do something about it, but we need to find a solution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madame Judge, I didn't ask for anything. The Prosecution has it in English. The problem is that they didn't provide you with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it seems that the Prosecution does not have the translation into English. Mr. Marcussen, could you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, we do not have a copy of the statement that's being shown on the screen now. That is the 1993 statement. However, the contents of that statement is exactly the same as the one from 2000 -- from 1992, so Your Honours can maybe refer to the translation of the 6 November 1992 statement for the translation. The only difference, as far as I know, is that there is one sentence added at the end of the 1993 statement which says that the witness is willing to give evidence before other courts or something to that effect, but otherwise the two statements are identical.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I had two possibilities before me, either to read the entire text or to summarise and save time, and look at the main points of paragraph 1. Since you do have it in English, then they could have placed the statement given to the Security Service in 1992. I assume that this is the statement given to the Centre for Research into War Crimes. They are identical; it's just been retyped. So, in fact, you do have the first paragraph in English. Now, if you want me to read all this out and then the interpreters can repeat it all, we can do that, but we'll lose a lot of time. Anyway, in paragraph 1, the witness describes his vision of the overall situation in Ilijas municipality and blames the leadership of the Serbian Democratic Party for everything that happened there, and there is absolutely no mention, not a single word, about Vasilije Vidovic coming with 24 Chetniks from Knin. And my point is this, and I'm going to ask the witness a question:

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Subsequently, you lied pursuant to somebody's instructions, that Vaske Vidovic came with 20 Chetniks from Knin; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not tell any lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's inappropriate to put to the witness he's lying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, before accusing anyone of lying, things are very complicated. It seems that there's a mystery; try and get to the bottom of things. You are right, in the 1992 statement this is not mentioned, so just ask him why, and why it crops up later on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already asked him that. I asked the question, and he didn't give me a direct answer. He's going on about something else, that Vaske Vidovic participated in an attack on his village, and we haven't got to the attack yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know who Samir Margetic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samir Margetic, I don't know the first name, Samir, but I do know the surname, Margetic, and I think it's Boro's brother, a man who was killed on the Knin battle front, and on the death certificate it said "Fell for his fatherland." And in Ilijas, we say "gave his life for the homeland."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. But do you know when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, he was killed while the fighting was going on in Kninska Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Ilijas at the time, everything was calm, but he was killed in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was killed in Benkovac during the fighting there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: After the Vance-Owen Plan, there was no fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Anyhow, that happened at the end of 1991, and you do know -- you are aware of the fact that at the funeral of Samir Margetic, Vaske Vidovic arrived with another five volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party from Knin, in fact from Benkovac, and you had heard they were there, perhaps you even saw them. Anyway, it was at the end of 1991. They arrived wearing uniforms. They had pistols at their belts, and at the funeral itself of Samir Margetic, a unit of the Yugoslav People's Army had a salvo -- a salute salvo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at the Margetic funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you must have known that that happened at the end of 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was killed. I saw the death announcements, but I don't remember the date of his death, when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. But do you know that Vaske Vidovic and another five volunteers arrived with travel documents of the JNA, giving them permission to carry weapons and setting out their destination and the reason for their travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. But, anyway, then the fact that these five volunteers, with Vaske Vidovic, were present at Samir Margetic's funeral at the end of 1991, you abused that fact to present a lie subsequently and state that Vaske Vidovic came with 20 Chetniks at quite a different period of time; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vaske Vidovic stayed in Ilijas with a group of 20 Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You lied about that subsequently, because nowhere in any of the records do we find the names of these Chetniks, and the Prosecutor could have come by those records. They could have had everything at their disposal. However, not a single Chetnik with Vaske Vidovic arrived in Ilijas when he returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the Judges are not saying that you lied. However, could it be possible that you confused things, that you mixed things up? It seems obvious that Vaske went to the funeral of Samir Margetic at the end of 1991, so they came all dressed up, with weapons. Mr. Seselj is stating it, so there's no reason to challenge this. Then later on, you see Vaske Vidovic again. So years later, did you say at the time, "Oh, they were there," and then later on you say, "Oh, they were also there when the village was attacked"? Is that what could have happened, or are you absolutely sure that Vidovic did come with the 20 Chetniks when this -- we know this from what you said on November 6, 1992, because at the time of course your recollection was better, so you could have said then that he was there with 20 Chetniks coming from Knin, but you don't say that in 1992. But maybe years later you said, "Well, he must have been there." So please tell us, are you 100 per cent sure or not so sure? We're not talking about lies, because that's another problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm certain, 100 per cent. I saw those people more than once. I saw them sitting and drinking in the tavern called Stella in Ilijas, over a month. They were there for over a month when I was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, when I was listening to you, I had a question in mind, and I'll ask it right now. These 20 people, if they stayed, where did they sleep? This is a question that I wanted to put to you yesterday, but now that I have an opportunity to ask it, I'll ask it. Where did they sleep, where did they reside? Okay, here you're saying that they're having coffee. Fine, but where do they sleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I said yesterday that they were accommodated, some of them in the apartment of Vasilije Vidovic and others in the house of Vasilije Vidovic in Podlugovi, which is a rather large house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, please resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the investigators of the ICTY in 2004, you did not say that these people were put up in the house and in the apartment of Vaske Vidovic. You said, instead, they were put up in a number of apartments.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way even now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You could put it any way you like; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One group was certainly in Vaske's apartment. Another group was certainly in the house at Podlugovi. I didn't go to count them, whether all of the 20 were sleeping at Vaske's address.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How could they have spent nights in the house in Podlugovi when it was not finished, that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true. It was finished. There was a restaurant on the ground floor, and there were rooms upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were not fit for inhabitation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go there, but my -- but his father and mother lived there for years. How could they have done that if the rooms were incomplete?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You stated that Vaske Vidovic drove away a whole transport of fuel belonging to the JNA from Visoko to Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The book, "The Nemanjici of Ilijas," written by a former judge of the Municipal Court in Ilijas, Velemir Adzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you read in that book that Vaske Vidovic drove away that transport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you're lying again, and I'll show now. Be so kind, we'll show one page by one on the ELMO. This is the book "The Nemanjici of Ilijas," and you'll see what kind of liar this witness is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The fact that the witness provides information which may not be completely the same as the information in the statements does not necessarily mean that he lies. Lying is a willful act of deception, and you must allow room for witnesses not being able to tell, with exact precision, the events that took place 15 years ago. So please refrain, professionally, from intimidating the witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I'm not intimidating anyone here. This witness never mentioned in his earlier statements any confiscation of oil transports from Visoko to Knin, and he said earlier in his testimony that it was done by Vaske Vidovic. And now he tells us he read that in the book of Velemir Adzic called "The Nemanjic Family in Ilijas." I got a hold of that book. Here you see the cover page. Can you turn the page, please, now? That is the blank page after the cover page. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So on this page, towards the top, it says it was well known that on the Knin theatre of war, there was participation by fighters from Ilijas, such as Vasilije Vidovic and others, and Margetic. In this theatre of war, the Serb units needed badly the fuel they did not have. That is why the military command of Ilijas dispatched one transport of fuel from depot 27 of the logistical base in Misoca, accompanied by members of this special unit. And then it goes on to enumerate 20 of them. Do you see their names? Do you see "Vaske Vidovic" anywhere? Go through the whole list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I'm sorry to intervene here again. I thought you were going to explain to me and to prove to me how the witness is lying, because to me, to be told that you are a liar, is intimidating. You can tell the witness that what he tells is incorrect, fine, and you can prove that what he says is incorrect. But if you're implying that he's lying, that's a criminal charge, you see, and there's a difference between not being able to put it -- to get it right, on the one hand, and, on the other hand, willfully lying to this Court. So again, acting as a professional counsel in court, you should refrain from intimidating a witness by calling him a liar, if you don't mean to have him charged with lying and deceiving justice. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am convinced, Judge, that you will prosecute him, as the Trial Chamber, because you've already been able to ascertain that he is lying. Why would I prosecute him? I cannot prosecute all the liars of this world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I have seen no signs of lying here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He invoked the book "The Nemanjic Family of Ilijas," that he read in that book that Vasilije Vidovic, also known as Vaske, drove away a transport of fuel from Misoca to Knin. I put to him that book, where you can see that it was not Vaske Vidovic who did that, that it was done by the JNA, that an NCO of the JNA headed that transport along with a special unit whose members are enumerated one by one. Vasilije Vidovic is not among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you found his name there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vasilije Vidovic is not mentioned here, but it doesn't mean he wasn't in Knin Krajina when the fuel was transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What are you saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading to you what it says. The Knin battlefield was well known in its participated fighting men from Ilijas, such as Vasilije Vidovic, Vaske, and Samir Margetic. In that theatre of war, the Serb units badly needed the fuel, so the Serb units needed fuel. It doesn't mean that Vasilije wasn't there. In this list of 20, he's not included, that much I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you said in examination-in-chief, and you said earlier in cross-examination again, that you read in this book that Vasilije Vidovic drove away a transport of fuel from Misoca to Knin. We have the book to which you referred, and you can see that you were not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read this text we're all looking at, I really read it, and I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I don't want to put you in a difficult situation, but I would like to pick up on what you said. You said that Vaske had taken part in some fuel transport, and this is what you said. Then you say that this seems to have been confirmed in a book that was written by someone, seemingly, and that this is not challenged. Now, Mr. Seselj reads this book and realises that there is a list of people who took part in this fuel transport in this book, and the name of Vaske is not mentioned. How can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read this book, and I noted that Vidovic was on this team. It's true that I didn't have the book itself. It was reprinted in certain publications. Maybe I did not read everything in detail, but I would like to read the book itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see the name under number 20 as part of this special unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What's the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marinko Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you maybe make a mistake, mistaking Marinko for Vasilije Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell. I would like to leaf through the book, if the Court allows it. I think that perhaps in the rest of the book, there might be another paragraph about this fuel transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says: "Fifteen days later," below, "another transport of fuel was dispatched to Banja Luka, and it was escorted by the following:" Then follows a list of 14 persons, headed by Radinko Ristic and other names. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this fuel transport was not to Knin, it was to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never discussed this, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We didn't. That's why it's important for me to say something about this now. In Misoca, there was a large depot of the JNA; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was a lot of fuel there used for wartime reserves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Two transports were sent from that depot within 15 days, one to Knin, another to Banja Luka; can you see this from this book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can it be seen that these fuel transports have nothing to do with Vasilije Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he should be involved in the first transport. I should need to look at the rest of the book. And we never discussed the second transport, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you can look at the rest of the book when you go home. We don't have time for that here now. Please return the book to me. Let's go back to your statement. Can the prior statement of the witness be put on the ELMO, please. After the general background information about the situation in Ilijas before the war, where you don't mention Vasilije Vidovic or the alleged arrival of 20 Chetniks from Knin, you move on to describe the conflicts in Ljesevo in the second paragraph. Is it the case that before this fighting in Ljesevo, there were some other skirmishes in the area of Ilijas municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of Ilijas municipality, you could hear shooting, but I don't know of any specific incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're not aware of the clash of the 3rd of May, where around 10 Serbs were killed? That was about a month earlier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of that fight, but I don't believe it was in Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the statement we saw yesterday by General Josipovic. I gave it to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness said that he had heard about the incident and he didn't -- but he didn't see it, so I doubt whether the statement which is going to be shown, which is about this incident, can take us any further. The witness has said he doesn't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, if the witness knows nothing about it, what is the point of addressing this issue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To establish, first of all, whether he is aware of it or not, Mr. President. The fact that he said at first blush that he didn't know about it does not mean anything. The purpose of cross-examination is to jog his memory and find that he maybe does know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know who General Josipovic is; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Josipovic was the commander of the barracks in Visoko, the man who withdrew the weaponry from the barracks in Visoko and distributed it to Serbs in Cekrcici, Ljesevo, Ljubnici, Podlugovi, and another place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But it was at a time when the Muslim leadership in Bosnia-Herzegovina had already violated the constitution, and despite the opposition of the Serbian people, declared independence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that they pulled out the weapons and distributed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Of course it was distributed to the loyal part of the population. Of course they're not going to leave it to the green ones in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whom do you call loyal?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, your community declared independence, anti-constitutionally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, that's an aggression of the Muslim leadership against Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's according to you. Bosnia-Herzegovina is an internationally-recognised state.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it was recognised by those who do as they please throughout the world, because they have the power.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers both slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am talking about events independently of international politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You talk about the arming of the Serb people. The Muslims were the first to arm themselves and declare independence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. The Prosecutor is on his feet. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It was primarily an attempt to get the witness and the accused to stop talking over each other. The accused cut off the witness in the middle of an answer. That was the first reason. The second reason is I don't think this line of questioning is relevant to the case at all. This is about crimes that were committed in a specific location, and this dispute between the two, the witness and the accused, about the political developments is irrelevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would like to tell both the witness and the accused to slow down. Now, as far as a connection between the crimes mentioned and the indictment, that Mr. Marcussen has stipulated that he doesn't see in what way this is relevant, it is for the accused to demonstrate this, please avoid political issues, current political issues. If you wish to discuss these, refer to the political situation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of the statement, you see that General Josipovic says that on the 3rd of May, 1995, an attack took place in Ilijas municipality from the directions of Visoko and Breza. Do you know of that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was an attack by the Muslim armed forces, and General Josipovic says that at the time the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Ilijas was used first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Ilijas municipality -- I was in Ilijas municipality. I wasn't in Breza or Visoko at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you should know that the pretext for the event was the -- or, rather, the cause of it was the situation in Ljesevo, that is to say, your village, and do you know that previously negotiations had taken place between the president of the municipality of Breza; have you heard of Salka Opacina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he the mayor of Breza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was Dr. Jevric in Ilijas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Dr. Jevric was nor do I know him at all. And I doubt that he's from Ilijas anyway. If he were from Ilijas, I would have known him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know there were negotiations conducted because Salka Opacina gave an ultimatum that the Serb population from Odzaci should hand over their weapons; do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, that's the first time I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And are Odzaci part of Ljesevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are two or three kilometres away from where my place is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it's the same local community, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Odzak and Ljesevo local communities, they are two settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But one local community, one local commune?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the majority of population in Odzaci was Serbs, right, and in Ljesevo Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Muslims of Ljesevo did have weapons, the Serbs in Odzaci had weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that the Muslims in Ljesevo did not have weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: First of all, let me say that before you, we had a witness here who said that the Muslims in Ljesevo did have weapons, but that some of them fled to Visoko and Breza with their weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that the Muslims of Ljesevo in my part of Ljesevo did not have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Judges, when we come to a situation like that, we have two witnesses testifying about the same situation, and one of them says the Muslims were armed, the other says the Muslims were not armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Seselj. I will first of all ask the Registrar to redact line 15, 16 and 17 of page 25, because one could perhaps identify the witness. I assume that Mr. Marcussen was on his feet for that same reason. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, I was on my feet because the accused started to make submissions rather than just putting questions. He made his case with respect to differences between testimony and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, put your questions and don't make statements. You know this as well as I do. Don't make any submissions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I drew your attention to the fact. If you're not interested in that, then I withdraw it, because we had a witness who said that the Muslims were armed, but some of them fled, and now we have a witness here who says that the Muslims weren't armed at all, and that is why this document is important to us. Here, General Josipovic claims that the meeting between Dr. Jevric and Salka Opacina was held on the 30th of April and that they didn't manage to reach any kind of agreement. And that on the 3rd of May, the attack began of the Patriotic League and Green Berets from three directions, Visoko, Banija, Ljubnici --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know where Ljubnici is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then the Visoko-Cekrcici-Odzak axis, and the Breza-Vrbovik-Odzaci axis, and the attack began with an artillery assault which lasted for 30 minutes, and you didn't hear that artillery attack at all, did you; is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could hear some of it, but for a short time and far away, not in Ljesevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, Ljesevo wasn't engulfed by that. We see the places that were, and the assault didn't last long, just 30 minutes. Now, here General Josipovic states that in the region of Feature 715, the village of Dobra -- do you know where the village of Dobra is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Dobra, it's the first time I'm hearing of it. Perhaps we have a different name for it, perhaps the village you mean is a village in the Visoko municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see. Now you have the names of nine Serbs who were killed on that occasion. Do you see that there, do you see the list of names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see the names of some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now turn to page 2. Zoom down, please. Thank you. Now, General Josipovic says the following: In the area of Odzaci, the village of Odzaci, which is the same municipality as Ljesevo, a battle went on for several hours. And that's two kilometres away from you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, on the village of Odzaci, from the back, and from the village of Ljesevo, it's the Muslim part so he thinks it's the same commune as well, fire was opened continuously. Do you know that from this village of Ljesevo in which you were too, do you know that they opened fire on Odzaci when Odzaci was attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no question of that whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you're denying it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No question of that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what about this: Do you know where Boric is, where it says the same region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: About 200 metres from Ljesevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, towards Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Anyway, General Josipovic says that it was from the Borici region that mortar support was provided at the village of Odzaci; that is to say that the Muslims attacked Odzaci with mortars; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wanted to say is this is funny, but I don't really --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, go ahead, just say it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. General Josipovic goes on to say the battle ended at 1800 hours of that same day and that a truce was agreed then, and that then intensive talks began about the Muslims surrendering weapons, Muslims from Ljesevo, because the Muslim attack on Odzaci was unsuccessful, they didn't manage to disarm the Serbs, and now it's the Serbs demanding that the Muslims be disarmed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was the request made for the Muslims of Ljesevo to be disarmed? Do you know that the Muslims from Ljesevo were asked to lay down their arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they surrendered their weapons, part of the police weapons that they had, and that all this was done in proper fashion. We discussed that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. You said yesterday that they surrendered their weapons, whereas a moment ago you said there were no weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you the kind of weapons there were yesterday, how many weapons and where the weapons came from and went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, it's quite obvious here that the Serb forces considered that the Muslims had not handed over all their weapons; isn't that right? We can see that from what General Josipovic writes here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what General Josipovic writes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, then the attack on Ljesevo started, and you said that it started on the 4th of June; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please remember to observe a small pause between question and answer. It is almost impossible for the interpreters to follow you, and the result is that we don't get your answer right, nor do we get the accused's questions right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you, yourself, said that the shooting went on for a long time on all sides; that you could hear explosions, grenades exploding, or as far as my information tells me, it was just mortar fire, not grenades. Anyway, you describe that in your statement. However, you keep quiet about one point, and it is this: That three Serbs were killed in that attack. Did you know that three Serbs were killed in the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And this particular Serb, Novo Rasevic, about whom you claim took he took part in your arrest, in fact was killed on that same day, as well as Miodrag Vukovic, Novo Rasevic and Budimir Stanisic, and you claim that Novo Rasevic took part in your arrest. And here General Josipovic states that they were killed at the doors of Arif Masnopita's house and that they were killed by Arif Masnopita and two other Muslims; is that correct? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it's not. May I be allowed to finish what I wanted to say? In our village, there was never a man called Arif Masnopita, and I doubt that there was one at that time. But you can check it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was his name, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Might it have been Atif?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that this killing took place at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you denying the fact that these people were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say -- I don't know about this killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is there a man called Atif Masnopita?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what about Asim Masnopita? Well, then it's Asim, and not Arif but Asim.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I doubt that. I don't believe this statement by Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you don't know]believe that the three Serbs were killed in Ljesevo that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assume that they might have been, but I don't know nothing -- I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And how can you say, then, that you recognised Novo Rasevic among the men who took you out of the shelter, who arrested you, captured you and took you away, when Novo Rasevic died in battle that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Novo Rasevic, if he was killed and if this is true, then he was killed after my arrest and transport to the camp.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now have the statement given back to me, the statement that the witness gave to the security services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, yesterday, as I was listening to you discussing the shooting, I wondered whether a battle hadn't pitched the Green Berets and the Muslims against the Serbs. I had no further information, but now it seems that three Serbs were killed. Unless they committed suicide or killed each other, we may well wonder whether these three Serbs were not killed by the opponent. That cannot be called into question. Now, it seems that, (a), among one of the people who arrested you, one of them has died. Did he die before or after? If he died before your arrest, then what you are saying poses a problem. If he died afterwards, this means that the shooting continued, the fighting continued. Witness, what can you say about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he was killed, he could have been killed after having arrested me. However, about any fighting or his death, I have absolutely no information. I don't know anything about that, because I'd already been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1055, the shelter you were arrested -- where you were arrested, how far is it from the place where 20 Muslims were executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between two and three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see, between two and three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Anyway, you state that this man, Ranko Draskic, was one of the men who arrested you, and the Prosecutor has presented data to the effect that Ranko Draskic had taken part in the execution of a group of 20 Muslims two or three kilometres further off from the place where, allegedly, he arrested you, so now I'm wondering this: This man Ranko Draskic, did he take part in your arrest or did he take part in the execution of the group of 20 Muslims? He couldn't have taken part in both events, so could the Prosecution clear up that problem and see what they're charging me with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place where I was arrested was quite certainly attacked from the Ilijas axis. Now, the forces -- the Serb forces of Vasilije Vidovic and his company, his group first of all captured us and then set off further afield. So that happened later that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's take a look at what you state in your statement. Have we got it on the overhead projector? You said yesterday that in the attack, the Serbs used their artillery; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was shooting there where mortars, shells, grenades were falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, mortars isn't part of our artillery weaponry. Did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you should have learned that mortars are infantry weapons, not artillery weapons. You should have learned that during your military service.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possibly. I say I don't know about that, but there were artillery pieces or weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So there were artilleries apart -- weapons apart from the mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, you say in your statement on the 4th of June, 1992, towards the evening in Ljesevo -- or, rather, shooting started at Ljesevo from all types of weapons. They opened fire from all sides, and "we saw that we had been surrounded and that serious things were -- and terrible things were taking place. Together with my brother and my neighbours, we were in front of Mahmut Fazlic's house, we fled to the cellar, and throughout that time they kept shooting at it. The chances of us escaping were negligible, because the whole area was attacked by Pans and other artillery weapons." So in 1992, in your statement there, no mention is made of artillery, and now you're adding -- no mention is made of artillery, and now you're adding it there. The more time goes by, you're going to introduce heavier weaponry in your statement and you'll end up with an atomic bomb, I don't doubt. Then you said: "We spent the night in great fear." So the shooting started towards evening, and the whole night you lived in fear. Now, if the Serbs started the shooting and if there was no response from the other side, no retaliation, why would they wait for a whole night? I assume they could have taken control of Ljesevo within 15 minutes, so it's quite obvious that the fighting went on throughout the night, the whole night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no question of any fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, why would the shooting have lasted the entire night, as you say, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were shooting. You should ask them why they were shooting, those Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, they were shooting because you did not wish to surrender your weapons, and two enemy armies cannot survive in one area. It's either one or the other that is going to win. You couldn't defeat them a month earlier, and now they came to defeat you; isn't that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see, it's not. So you use -- you were using the proverb that the anthropologists found in some African tribe at a very low level of development. "It's a good thing when we attack the neighbouring tribe, kill the menfolk, take the womenfolk away, their property, and it's bad when they attack us and kill our menfolk and take our womenfolk away." That's the same logic that you apply. A war happened, and there were crimes committed on both sides in a war, and I don't justify the crimes that took place in Ljesevo. Both sides get killed and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you're making submissions again. I'm sure Mr. Marcussen was about to say this. You're making submissions. There's challenge on artillery, on the fighting. Of course, the Judges noted this. It did not escape them. Witness, please, you're saying that when you were with other people, when you spend the night with them, you heard artillery shots, but as far as you know there was no fight. Your friends did not shoot, there were no Green Beret, there were no Muslim units fighting against the Serbs at that time. At least that's what you're saying; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You go on to describe how you spent the whole night in fear because of that firing. In the morning, you heard Chetnik voices. So in your eyes, all the Serb soldiers were Chetniks; no discussion about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men who arrested us were Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. And you say that you expected them to enter the basement. Some of you attempted to escape. They gave up. And when the Chetniks arrived, you got out, with your arms in the air. They jumped you immediately and fell you to the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you said the Chetniks were led by Vasilije Vidovic, nicknamed Vaske. You were not quite so emphatic here that he was there on the spot outside your shelter. You say he led the Chetniks, and one draws the conclusion that he actually led the attack on the village; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vasilije was outside our basement, as I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, let's see when you lied, either in 1992 or yesterday. You say that the Chetniks ordered you to look down, but still you recognised them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, don't say "let's see when you lied." First make a demonstration, and at the end you could say, "Did you say the truth, "yes" or "no, rather than saying from the onset, "You lied and I'm going to prove it to you."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say you recognised four men, Vlajko Lizdek, nicknamed Vlaja, Novo Rasevic, Novo Panjic, and Ranko Draskic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We've seen that Novo Rasevic died that day, got killed, whereas the other three were never part of Vaske's unit. Let's take, please, the lists that we had with the previous witness, the list of members of those three platoons of the Territorial Defence Company. I have it somewhere here if you don't have it. Here are the lists. Are you sure that you recognised Ranko Draskic among the four?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you show him the lists, one by one, and we'll stop on the third list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let me inform you immediately, I have lists of members of the Territorial Defence from Ljesevo. It's three platoons. This is the first list. Turn to the next page. The second and the third lists. Towards the bottom, it says: "Commander of the 3rd Platoon, Ranko Draskic." This list is dated 16 May 1992. Ranko Draskic is commander of the 3rd Platoon, whereas Vasilije Vidovic was commander of a special platoon later known as Vaske's Platoon. We'll see that from other documents. How could have Ranko Draskic been under the command of Vasilije Vidovic when they were not in the same unit at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They jointly attacked the village with joint forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If they attacked with joint forces, then each unit must have been deployed in a certain place. Their soldiers did not mix, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1055 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They attacked the village with joint forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have here up to page 78. It's much more than I will show you. I have the workbook, the log of Vaske's Platoon, and on the cover page we see the title: "The Wounded and the Fallen." And on page 22, "Tasks for the Soldiers," and at the end -- do you have this? I gave it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor is on his feet. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I was just going to ask the accused to let us know where this document can be found so we can follow. I am guessing that it's from the binder that he has indicated he's going to use, but what tab?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which tab is it under, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's tab 1, and the document is the one we'll look at now, pages 78 and 79. So could you please put them on the ELMO. It contains a list of all the members of the unit commanded by Vaske in 1992. On that list, none of the four names of the men the witness claims arrested him can be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, help us. We have three binders. Tell us which binder -- in which binder it is and where it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, this is binder number 1. It's marked "D1." So in the binders, you will find the documentation I presented to you during the testimony of the military expert. It contains evidence that Vasilije Vidovic, Ranko Dobrilovic [as interpreted] and a third one were continuously either in the JNA or the Army of Republika Srpska throughout the war, and they were part of the units of those armies. You refused to admit it into evidence. However, it is useful for me to at least show this witness one of these documents, because this is a workbook of Vasilije Vidovic from 1992. You can have the original for your inspection, if you wish. It's kept by my very good friend, whom I trust implicitly, in Belgrade. Vasilije Vidovic, he provided me with all that. It's a list of 54 members of his unit from 1992. And could the witness please find the four names of the men he claims were commanded by Vasilije Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the list. It's a handwritten list with 54 names, starting with "Vidovic, Vasilije" as number 1. And there's a number. It must be the ID of the soldiers or fighters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, these are probably numbers of their military service booklets. You have, at the end, six men without these numbers. They probably didn't do their military service yet at the time or didn't have these service books. Please go through the whole list. You will see that Vlajko Lizdek, Novo Rasevic, Novo Panjic, and Ranko Draskic are not there. Turn to the next page, please, for the witness to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it would seem -- it would seem that there are dates on these lists, and if Your Honours look, they seem to be lists from the 10th of May, 1995. So it's well after the time period that we are talking about here. This is a good reason why the accused should be requested to give us precise indications of the documents that he used so we can be able to detect these sort of things in time so we don't waste time on them in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Prosecutor is telling us that there might be a mix-up with this list, at least regarding the date. What elements do you have that could prove that this list of 54 people corresponds to the very period when these fights occurred in that town?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, on page 2 you have the date, 4th April, 1992, on page 2, and what is added in hand was in 1995. Do you see this on the sideline, on the margin? Well, this is the workbook of Vaske Vidovic that he used throughout the war, and this is a list of soldiers ending with September 1992. This has all been torn from one workbook to be presented here, so you can see easily what was entered at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the time might be up for the break, so maybe we can verify this, but it seems to me that this is a chronological workbook that runs through an extended period of time, and the part of the book that is now being presented to the witness concerns a period that's subsequent to the incident that we are talking about in the indictment. But maybe we can look at this closer during the break. The accused might want to check this, and we can look at it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to tell you this: This is a book that Vaske Vidovic kept throughout the war. Maybe it's a bit scruffy, but it's complete. You see, you even have shifts and replacements from 1992, ending with September. So when the soldiers went to positions, rotating, it's all recorded. It's obviously a workbook divided by topic. But everything that Vaske Vidovic wrote down during the war in this workbook, it's authentic, historic material. His unit began to self-organise and was joined in June to the Ilijas Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska. But what's important is that nowhere in the book will you find a person who is not from Ilijas or one of the surrounding places. It's important, because Vasilije Vidovic never had any volunteers from Serbia. You can see this from the workbook. The witness can go through the list and see if there is a single name of a person who is not from his locality. He knows these surnames; he should, at least, like Serbs know Muslim surnames.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. During the break, the Prosecutor will have time to delve into this. I believe that he must delve into the entire first binder. There are page numbers, and we see that there are other pages with dates and so forth and so on. Well, we'll have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have 45 minutes left. Go ahead. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to the accused using this list in the way he's trying to use the document, or the workbook that he was using with the witness before the break. From my review of the dates that can be found in the various documents, it would appear that these records do not date from the time that's relevant to the witness evidence. Now, I don't -- yeah, basically the accused would have to call Vasilije Vidovic here to explain to the Court what these records are. It's very difficult to see, but the dates that are found in all of the workbooks seem to be from 1994-1995, where there are dates, or from -- clearly from months that are not relevant to the time frame that this witness is giving evidence about. And I can go into that in more detail, if Your Honours would like, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I looked at pages 78 and 79. You said that there was a date that could prove that this was in 1992. I looked for it desperately and couldn't find it. The Prosecution is raising a very serious objection, saying that according to him, this does not correspond to the period where the witness was -- it doesn't correspond to the period where the witness actually was in Vaske in places, so there is doubt. So how are you saying that you're so sure that this list of 54 names corresponds to those who are actually there when all these events that we're interested in occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you should then look through the whole book, the whole notebook, because it is a notebook in which everything important was recorded from 1992 until 1996, when the Serbs left Ilijas after the Dayton Accords. So take a look at page 5, for example. You'll find the name "Srdjan Kalas" there, son of Radoslav. He said -- received a decoration medal from Major Tepic by decree of Karadzic, and then was killed in the action to liberate Misoca in August 1992, for example, killed by an enemy shell. The previous page, there's another name there, a man called Slavko, with no other information provided. The page before that is a page that relates to Nadan Andric, and page 1 -- or, rather, number 2, as it is here, Vasilije Vidovic, who was commander of that platoon, and his military post 7419/17 [as interpreted] is mentioned, and his platoon had a separate military post, 7491/17. And if you go on after page 5, you have Slavko Kulac, Dragan, killed at Zuc in November 1992. Then you come across someone else on page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just ask you, Mr. Seselj, if you go back to page 2, where Vidovic's details were, you made reference to the number on the top of the page, 7491/17. At the bottom of that page, there's a date, "8 June 1995." Would that not suggest that this entry was made in June 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. You have it in English. Quite right. This was added on in 1995, and it says: "During combat, the following was wounded in the right leg by an enemy shell 8th of June, 1995." And this notebook refers to all those years. It's the only working notebook or diary kept by Vasilije Vidovic or, rather, this soldier, Nadan Andric, whose name and particulars are on page 3 and this is his handwriting. So over those few years, he recorded everything that was most important for that platoon. All the soldiers who were in the platoon are recorded there whenever they became members of the platoon, then those who were killed, those who were wounded, what weapons were issued to them, and so on and so forth. And you can look at the entire notebook and find all that information. Perhaps it wasn't kept in the best possible way, it's not a neat notebook, but it contains a lot of information. You can see here, for example, that Vasilije Vidovic joined the Army of Republika Srpska on the 4th of April, 1992. That is recognised there. And then later on you have a photocopy of his military booklet, where you have the same information, when he was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, his years of service there are recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If I understand this correctly, the issue is whether the list that is included in pages 78 and 79 was included in the book in 1992 or at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to Vidovic, this whole integral list was compiled in September 1992. But before this list, if you look at it, there's one name on every page, so that was the primary composition of the unit until page 14 -- or 13, rather. You have just one name per page. Later on, you have a number of names on one page, from page 14 onwards, page 15 and so on. But when you look at the whole notebook, you'll notice that it contains all the names of the men who were ever in Vasilije Vidovic's unit. So the Prosecutor can look at all the names recorded in the book to see where they came from, whether they were from Ilijas and the surrounding parts or from somewhere else, from Serbia perhaps. So I can't put this notebook in the order in which I would like it to look. It looks in the authentic way that it was written, that's what it is, so what you see is what you get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my respectful submission, we cannot be satisfied that the list that the accused wants to put to the witness reflects the composition of the unit at the relevant time. Judge Harhoff has already pointed to page 2, where there's a date, 8 June 1995. At page 7 -- sorry, that's incorrect. If Your Honours go to page 12, you will see that that appears to be a record that's made on the 3rd of October, 1994. The record on page 13 seems to be describing events on the 11th of April, 1995. For example, page 20 is about something that happened on the 12th of October -- sorry, about something on the 4th of August, 1994. If we look at the workbook that's found under tab 3, which begins at page 59, Your Honours will see that there are no names -- sorry, there are no years mentioned there, but it seems to be a record that pertains to something that occurred between the 28th of September, in an unknown year, so not the relevant month, until December at some year. If Your Honours look at page 71, you will again see -- which is, of course, a few pages before the pages that the accused wants to use with the witness, we have a date, the 14th of October, 1995. Then, of course, we have, on page 77, the date that I mentioned earlier, the 10th of August, 1995. And if Your Honours then go to the subsequent pages, the next book that's found under -- or two books, the book that I found under tab 7, at page 87, we have a whole series of entries from 1995, beginning on the 26th of June, 1995. So in my respectful submission, it would appear that these records have been made subsequent to the events, and certainly we cannot be satisfied that the lists that the accused wants to put to the witness, seemingly to impeach him, is a record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, we understood you. As things stand, Mr. Seselj, the Trial Chamber has suspicions as to this list. It is it seem that this -- whether this list does correspond to 1992, and this for several reasons. First, I note that this notebook was -- there are different entries in this notebook made by different people, because we have all sorts of handwritings. Secondly, there is no order to the pages. Page 79, which you seem to say is an essential document as far as your case is concerned because it's a list of people, and then if you move to page 80, the next page, you find out that here there is a date and it's 1995, March 1st, 1995. So there is a big problem here, which means that between page 79 and page 80, three years were spent with no entries whatsoever. So there is suspicion on this document. It does not mean that I'm saying that this list does not date back to 1992, but there are great uncertainties about it. Ask your questions, please, and we will assess the answers, taking into account all these parameters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also wanted to say that on page 76, the list starts with number 18, whereas on page 73, it ends with number 10. And there's also a number 11, but it's left blank. Regarding 74, there's no number. Regarding page 75, no number either. So there, again, we're jumping from the 10th to the 18th, so it's very puzzling.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can be understood here for certain is the information recorded there, the entries made, and let's take page 20 that the Prosecutor referred to. The entry there is that Branislav Stojanovic was killed at Toljenka [phoen] on the 4th of August, 1994. So something is missing there, and what is missing might have been pulled out of the notebook.
